title: XIII-XVI: goodness, benignity, grace, mercy
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): so mercy stands as its third progression, finding a remedy toward ye miserable — just as grace stands as ye second progression belonging toward divine goodness excluding merit. Titus 3:5. Ephesians 2:4; Romans 9:18; here in ye former way — Exodus 34:6; Gods mercy stands as taken actively or passively; nothing obstructing by means belonging toward reason belonging toward sin — gods mercy stands as ye affection belonging toward coming to ye aid belonging toward ye miserable. XVI. prevenient, concomitant plus subsequent, sufficient plus efficacious, we treat elsewhere — distinctions belonging toward grace into operating plus cooperating. Grace excludes ye creatures merit; regarding none belonging toward their merits — grace stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God imparts some good to intelligent creatures. XV. another special toward ye elect. Matthew 5:45; one general toward all creatures — Psalm 145:9; The first progression belonging toward divine goodness stands as benignity; by means belonging toward giving some good, shows Himself beneficent to His creatures — benignity stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God. XIV. against ye heresy belonging toward Cerdo, Marcion, plus ye Manichees. Genesis 1:31; Luke 18:19; Matthew 19:17; That God stands as good, besides Scripture, all His works testify — Psalm 34:9; Goodness stands as that same by means belonging toward that same which God inclines toward communicating good outside Himself. XIII.
pass_b_english: XIII. Goodness is that by which God inclines toward communicating good outside Himself. That God is good, besides Scripture, all His works testify — Psalm 34:9; Matthew 19:17; Luke 18:19; Genesis 1:31; against the heresy of Cerdo, Marcion, and the Manichees.

XIV. Benignity is that by which God, by giving some good, shows Himself beneficent to His creatures. The first progression of divine goodness is benignity; one general toward all creatures — Psalm 145:9; Matthew 5:45; another special toward the elect. XV. Grace is that by which God imparts some good to intelligent creatures, regarding none of their merits. Grace excludes the creatures merit; distinctions of grace into operating and cooperating, prevenient, concomitant and subsequent, sufficient and efficacious, we treat elsewhere.

XVI. Gods mercy is the affection of coming to the aid of the miserable, nothing obstructing by reason of sin. Gods mercy is taken actively or passively; here in the former way — Exodus 34:6; Romans 9:18; Ephesians 2:4; Titus 3:5. Just as grace is the second progression of divine goodness excluding merit, so mercy is its third progression, finding a remedy for the miserable.
source_text: XIII. Bonitas est, qua Deus ad bonum extra se communicandum propendet. Bonum esse Deum praeter Scriptura omnia ipsius opera testantur — Psal. XXXIV.9; Matth. XIX.17; Luc. XVIII.19; Gen. I.31; contra Cerdonis, Marcionis et Manichaeorum haeresin. XIV. Benignitas est, qua Deus boni aliquid donando se creaturis suis beneficum exhibet. Primus divinae bonitatis progressus est benignitas; alia generalis erga omnes creaturas — Psal. CXLV.9; Matth. V.45; alia specialis erga electos. XV. Gratia est, qua Deus creaturis intelligentibus, nulla earum merita spectans, bonum aliquod impertit. Gratia excludit meritum creaturae; distinctiones gratiae in operantem et cooperantem, praevenientem, concomitantem et subsequentem, sufficientem et efficacem alibi expendimus. XVI. Misericordia Dei est affectus miseris, nihil obstante peccato, subveniendi. Misericordia Dei vel active accipitur vel passive; priore modo hic — Exod. XXXIV.6; Rom. IX.18; Eph. II.4; Tit. III.5. Sicut gratia est secundus bonitatis divinae progressus excludens meritum, ita misericordia est tertius illius progressus, remedium miseris inveniens.
